description: The first family-F27 arm (DECISIONS.md 9.146): three physical identities the F26 gate exposed, each shipped as a declared value whose control member reproduces F26 exactly. (1) A household drives the cars the census gives it - B.population.vehicle_roster = census maps every licensed, car-available member of a household to one of its householdVehicles shared cars, hh<id>_car<k>, and RUN.qsim.vehicle_behavior = wait holds the second driver at the link until the car returns; at the F26 gate 12,317 car legs (3.28% of resident car legs, 5,279 households, 4,265 of them one-car households with two members out at once) began while every car the household owns was already out, and 29,827 of 107,526 declared bound trips were driven by the passenger themselves. (2) The coherence listener re-proposes DECLARED pairs only - B.ride.coherence_scope = declared - where before it inferred pairs from endpoints and clock for anyone in the household: 12,461 of 66,909 selected ride legs at the F26 gate sat on persons the demand never bound, proposed at ~5,000 an iteration while GatedSubtourModeChoice refused 192,000 of the same kind, and those were the legs that never paired (miss_declared_absent 719 against 16,527 unpaired). (3) A motorbike or truck carve never draws a bound passenger, in the pool solve and at the draw: 373 sampled locked persons held bound trips and 571 were selected as the lock's mode. What the arm must answer, in order. (a) THE ROSTER: car legs starting with every household car out (0 expected for one-car households), the wait-time distribution, stuck agents attributable to a car that never came back, and where the 29,827 self-driven bound trips settle - onto ride, walk or pt. (b) THE LISTENER: ride legs on persons with no boundDriver (~0 expected) and the pair rate against F26's 0.7865. (c) RIDE against -41.6%, read TOGETHER with car (+11.5%), walk (-22.7%), bike (+118.1%) and taxi (+157.0%): a real ride gain should draw car down and, if the car-less quarter's excess is ride's deficit (9.123), bike and taxi with it; walk left the band the wrong way at F26 as car took its trips, so the seesaw is the thing to watch. (d) The bound-trip selection rate against F26's 0.455 - the selection half of the lane, which is what remains once the second car is gone. (e) The pt SPLIT as a CONTROL: heavy rail +234.7%, bus +40.5%, light rail -55.9%, ferry -70.5% at F26; nothing here touches pt. (f) CONVERGENCE, requirement 8, still unmeasured: innovation off at 240. (g) The awaiting-run measurements the open issues name: #145, #86, #48, #93, #96, #94, #98, #108, #107, #82, #131, #30, #49, #50, #66. S2 x WEEKDAY at 25%, 300 iterations, innovation off at 240, gated every 100 iterations under the loop in GOAL.md with the runner's own watcher stopping the hard bar itself (9.137) - in which case the arm closes itself out as stopped_at_gate and its reading is citable at its reached_iteration and nowhere past it (9.143). 25% is the standing directive (user, 1 Sep). Cost: MEASURED, not projected - the F26 arm took 38,426 s to iteration 100, a mean 384 s an iteration, so 300 iterations is ~32 h; `wait` adds waiting agents to the qsim and may move that either way, and the first 25% arm with a shared vehicle is the measurement of it. Graph rendering is OFF (9.59). NEVER compare this arm with any run before the F27 boundary: the demand (householdVehicles, the carve pool), the plans and the compiled controler are all part of a run's identity (9.127, 9.138, 9.142, 9.143, 9.146). NOTHING THIS PRODUCES IS A RESULT until its record says ran_to_last_iteration.
